newsitem.title: USA: Reputed mob boss Gigante released on bail in N.Y.
newsitem.headline: Reputed mob boss Gigante released on bail in N.Y.

text.p: Reputed mob boss Vincent "Chin" Gigante was released on $1 million bail from New York Downtown Hospital in Manhattan where he has been held under 24-hour guard for more than a month, officials said Thursday.

The reputed head of the Genovese crime family is now under house arrest at the home of his girlfriend on East 77 Street after U.S. District Judge Jack Weinstein restored his bail. Gigante is due to appear in court starting June 23 on federal charges of racketeering, running the Genovese crime family and ordering six murders.
On Tuesday, Weinstein ruled that Gigante was mentally competent to stand trial. He had been held under 24-hour guard for fear he would be sprung by associates.

A spokesman for the federal court Thursday said Gigante would wear an electronic monitoring bracelet and would be allowed to walk only within one block of girlfriend Olympia Esposito's posh East Side apartment.
Prosecutors objected to Gigante's release from the hospital, arguing that there was a risk he would flee.
He was indicted seven years ago but his trial has been repeatedly postponed because of competency hearings requested by his lawyers who claim he suffers from dementia and other ills.
